chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the child of fornication: should I buy him, sell him, or employ him? He said: 'Buy him, manumit him (make him a freed slave), employ him, and sell him. As for the foundling, do not buy him.'

key_terms.اِسْتَرِقَّهُ: Manumit him (grant freedom while retaining ownership)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling the child of fornication in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic status of the child of fornication (walad al-zina), affirming their eligibility for enslavement and trade, thereby distinguishing them from the foundling (laqit) who is not purchased. This ruling reflects the classical Shia view that walad al-zina are treated similarly to other slaves in terms of property rights, a nuance critical for understanding inheritance and manumission dynamics in early Shia fiqh. The distinction underscores the practical application of lineage and status in determining legal capacities within the household economy of the time.
